text:
alice: heads up — seeing a ~3x spike in reconnects from eu-west after the v2-proxy canary rolled out this morning
ben: timeline? which canary ID?
alice: deploy-bot reports v2-proxy canary started at 09:12 UTC, errors start ~09:18
deploy-bot: canary v2-proxy (rev=2026.03.18-canary) started at 2026-03-18T09:12:00Z
carla: what do the responses look like? 5xx or client disconnects?
alice: odd — clients attempt resume, backend returns 200 with body and x-resume-id preserved, but proxy replies to client with 204 No Content and drops x-resume-id header. sample from proxy access log + raw socket: 
```
PROXY -> client: HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:18:42 GMT
Connection: keep-alive


```
backend log: 
```
200 /stream/resume?user=42 headers={x-resume-id: abcd-1234} body=...
```
alice: so resume token never reaches client, client gives up and reopens a full session (quota spike).
ben: that explains the billing bump. console resume_count metric flat but stream_opened doubled. telemetry mismatch = console_resume_count vs prometheus stream_resume_total?
carla: can we reproduce locally by hitting proxy with a fake backend that sends chunked body and resume header?
alice: yes repro in staging — proxy returns 204 when backend sends Content-Length: 0 or when upstream connection had zero-length chunk before header flush. looks like an edge case in our response-headers->client flusher.
infra-bot: started a debug trace on one of the canary nodes (node-17).
ben: quick mitigation: pause canary and roll back, or update proxy to not transform 200+empty-body into 204. which is safer?
carla: temporary rollback asap. we need time to patch the proxy to forward headers even if body is empty.
alice: agreed — rolling canary back now. also filing follow-up to add e2e test for resume-token passthrough.
ben: also console UX: the resume panel hides sessions marked as resumed only if client reported resume event. since proxy strips header, console incorrectly marks these as cold opens. we should annotate the dashboard with upstream->proxy header drops in the service map.
carla: created ticket INF-4421: "proxy: preserve x-resume-id and avoid 204 conversion on empty bodies" and added test+canary plan. link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-4421
alice: for telemetry, adding a delta metric: proxy_forwarded_resume_total and an alert if (stream_resume_total - proxy_forwarded_resume_total) / stream_resume_total > 0.05 in a 5m window.
ben: also add a console note during rollouts: "proxy canary may temporarily affect resume metrics" — reduce pager noise.
alice: rollback completed, canary paused. initial numbers dropping back to baseline. I'll follow up with a small patch to ensure headers are forwarded before any body-length heuristic transforms status.
carla: nice triage. postmortem when fixed. :thumbsup:
ben: thanks — follow-up action items summarized: rollback, INF-4421 created, add e2e resume token test, add proxy_forwarded_resume metric, console notice during rollout.
alice: putting a short blameless postmortem on the board and assigning owners. ping me on this thread if you see anything else.
carla: FYI, edge case note for networking team: proxies that coalesce empty upstream frames can accidentally switch to 204 if they treat an initial zero-length body as terminal. will add to docs.
infra-bot: debug trace archived: s3://redwood-debug/node-17/proxy-trace-1777777777.tar.gz
